body:
Tested on 4.4 stable, 4..5 stable and latest master v4.6.beta.custom_build [f0aeea26f]. Seems to only happens if the autoload is created using a scene with a built-in script, otherwise seems to work as expected. Here the MRP i used for test: [test-parse-error.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24416473/test-parse-error.zip) The editor tooltip of the function is able to recognize the parameters and the return type, so in theory the parser should be able to do the same.

Also, no error is shown if you remove the variable typing and attempt to pass an invalid type to the function.

It's pretty unstable and would sometimes work in some code locations, but today I just added a new export var `first_room` above my other autoload class `InGameManager` member `player_character` and suddenly the parser showed error on every

```gd
var player_character := InGameManager.player_character
```

that I had to change to (workaround in OP)

```gd
var player_character: PlayerCharacter = InGameManager.player_character
```

So it's like the order in which it parses things and the context of member definition and calls seems to affect the result...

Noteworthy is that the autocomplete works in this case (in related issue we mention that sometimes autocomplete is also broken altogether, although that may be more a code editor interface thing e.g. VS Code plugin may make it work? Will try next time)

EDIT: if you got notified by GitHub of a new post and see nothing new here, it's normal, I had posted a wrong report which was irrelevant so I deleted that post.
If you're curious about what my mistake was: I forgot to strictly type my variable:

```gd
var room = instance.get_node("Room") as Room  # I forgot to use `:=` instead of `=`
var area_data := room.area_data  # Error: Cannot infer the type of "area_data"
```
